I added a 0.25-second sleep after each sandbox call in `tests/test_payments.py`. That limits the test to about 4 requests per second, just under the sandbox's 5 per second. The delay is stored in a named constant, `SANDBOX_CALL_INTERVAL`, with a comment explaining it, so it's easy to change. The test now takes about one second longer.

I didn't run the test, since it calls the real sandbox. Whether this fixes the CI flakes will only show over the next few CI runs.

The sleep only spaces out calls within this one test. If CI runs tests in parallel, or other tests also call the sandbox, they could still go over the limit together. In that case, a shared throttle or retrying when the sandbox returns 429 (too many requests) would be more reliable.

I also saved the sandbox's 5-requests-per-second limit to the project's memory (EngramDB), so future sessions will know about it.
